prompts.cover_burgundy:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: a proposed new antique cloth book front cover for Queen's Trial, image for art-direction review, not a game screenshot.
Input images: image 1 is ONLY the binding/material and gold drawing STYLE reference: the green cloth book with the gold dragon. Image 2 is the EXACT Queen character identity reference, a screenshot of this game's Queen; image 3 is her silhouette and dark clothing reference; image 4 is the protagonist, used ONLY for the muted burgundy-red cloth color.
Primary request: a much simpler authentic cloth-bound cover, WITHOUT ANY TITLE, LETTERS, NUMBERS OR MONOGRAMS. Replace green cloth with deep wine burgundy red, slightly plum-dark like the protagonist's cloak. Visible finely woven bookcloth / buckram threads and softly uneven dyed fibers, tactile matte fabric, not leather, not solid digital color. One delicately printed pale antique gold ink illustration integrated into the fabric, with fine slightly imperfect hand-engraved / hand-inked lines like image 1, restrained flat two-color craftsmanship. Gold is real-looking matte stamping with tiny ink skips across the weave, NOT shiny 3D metal.
Subject of gold drawing: the actual Queen from this game, recognizable by her enormous asymmetric spreading headdress made of overlapping long golden feather / leaf forms, with small open eyes embedded throughout the feather forms; her natural human nose and lips show below while her upper face and eyes are covered; high dark robe collar and long elegant robe silhouette. She is NOT a chess piece, NOT a conventional crowned fantasy queen, NOT an ordinary winged woman. Translate that specific identity into gold line art on the burgundy cloth.
Pose/composition: a graceful active three-quarter figure with her arms sweeping around TWO ROUND PLANETS THAT ARE COLLIDING, two distinct spherical outlines touching and breaking at their contact, etched fracture arcs, a beautiful curling current of fine planet fragments and stardust rising through the upper half of the cover and echoing the elongated sweeping line of the reference dragon. The collision is a poetic cosmological fable, drawn entirely as sparse gold ink, no photorealistic fireball. Let some fine orbital lines thread between her many-eyed feathers and the two worlds. One unified asymmetrical vertical narrative engraving with ample bare burgundy cloth around it, not a centered circular crest.
Framing: perfectly front-facing full book cover in portrait proportions about 2:3, slight binding seam at left, corners visible, modest straight edges, NO ornate border, NO corner fittings, NO jewelry, NO gems, NO embossed medallion, NO gilded page title cartouche. No text anywhere, no logos. No dragon, no castle, no generic zodiac wheel. Physical vintage textile binding with a handmade drawn motif; avoid slick digital fantasy illustration, plastic rendering, airbrush, gradients in the illustration, floating magical glow, ornamental stock borders. Book alone, clean small margins, genuinely transparent background around the silhouette.
prompts.first_edict:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one new COLOR illustration for the Queen's Trial tutorial book, for art-direction REVIEW only. This is a real-looking hand-drawn and hand-painted narrative plate on slightly warm ivory paper, NOT a screenshot and NOT a glossy digital fantasy painting.
Input images: Image 1 is ONLY the drawing and traditional painting STYLE reference: the colored illustration on the left page of the small book, not the photograph of hands, not the garden subject. Image 2 is the game's true cosmic world: a suspended black-and-white marble trial platform in a galaxy, floating planets, nebulae, a huge enigmatic Queen. Image 3 is the actual burgundy-hooded protagonist's identity, costume and color reference; Image 4 is the Queen's precise face/headdress identity if she is present. These game screenshots supply identity and universe ONLY, never their 3D rendering style.
Medium and craft: very evident expressive brown-black dip-pen contours, varied pressure, imperfect organic curved edges, tiny broken hatch marks and stippling. Watercolor and a little matte gouache applied by hand inside the ink drawing: uneven pigment pooling, granulation, dry-brush skips, areas of exposed paper, imperfect color registration, flat colored passages. The visual handwriting of a printed antique illustrated tale, like the supplied plate. Restrained, coherent colors: muted deep indigo and petrol-blue space, warm amber, moss/verdigris in the planets, ivory marble, wine-burgundy protagonist clothing. Colorful yet quiet, NOT sepia monochrome. No smooth gradient shading, no bloom, no polished reflective material, no airbrush, no cinematic volumetric light, no glossy game-concept rendering.
Queen identity when used: human lower face (nose and lips) visible, upper face hidden beneath a wide asymmetric cluster of long overlapping feather/leaf forms studded with little blue eyes, high dark robe collar. Do not replace her with a chess queen, a conventional crown or a winged princess.
Protagonist identity when used: the same dark burgundy-plum hood and elaborate long cloak of the screenshot, face a shadow under the hood, slender adult proportions. Show him from the back or three-quarter back if helpful.
Composition: a poetic, symbolic but concrete scene belonging ENTIRELY to this game's galaxy; portrait plate around 2:3, a strong asymmetrical narrative silhouette, calm ivory margins and visible hand-painted paper texture. Interpret the mechanics through cosmic imagery and gesture, never reproduce a solved grid or game interface. No castle, no towers as medieval buildings, no landscapes with trees, no mountains, no terrestrial river, no dragon, no generic fantasy village, no random decorative filigree. No text, no letters, no numbers, no interface, no logos, no frame. Scene: the hooded protagonist begins a small journey over a handful of ivory and charcoal marble squares suspended among constellations, only FOUR loose stepping tiles rather than a full board. A SINGLE cream edict card with an understated hand-painted zodiac motif floats just above his raised hand. His next footstep almost touches the nearest tile; a delicate winding trail of star specks carries the eye forward. A blue-green planet and a much smaller ochre planet interrupt a sparse indigo watercolor nebula in the distance. The Queen's recognizable many-eyed golden headdress appears only faintly in the far upper celestial wash, as the source of the decree. The scene communicates one decree and counting one's steps, without literal arrows or a puzzle answer.

prompts.page_design:
Use case: ui-mockup. Asset: a single proposed open-book tutorial page spread for Queen's Trial, art-direction REVIEW image only. Generate a beautiful physical illustrated book spread viewed directly from above, landscape approximately 3:2, both pages fully visible, modest margins around the book. No hands, no room, no table props, no surrounding scene. Genuine transparent background outside the book.
Input images: image 1 is ONLY the style and understated physical page/bookcraft reference (the photographed little illustrated book). Image 2 is the new approved-for-review colored illustration plate for the FIRST tutorial; reproduce this SAME hand-inked watercolor scene on the RIGHT page with recognizable burgundy protagonist, the single edict, floating black-and-white marble tiles, many-eyed Queen and galaxy. Image 3 is ONLY the burgundy woven binding material/color reference; do not put its gold cover illustration inside the pages.
Primary request: a more authored and warm storybook design with clear information, compared with a plain block of tutorial text. LEFT page is a short tutorial; RIGHT page is the colored hand-made painting. Natural ivory uncoated paper, visible fine paper grain, gentle central gutter and a few layered page edges, burgundy cloth binding just visible under the paper. Calm paper with subtle age, no burnt edges, no overly stained parchment and no thick stock decorative border.
Typography: large expressive dark-burgundy old-English blackletter heading on the LEFT, reserved ONLY for the heading; body lettering is a very readable organic humanist book serif with calligraphic rhythm (Alegreya-like), open lowercase, varied stems, generous leading, NOT Old English in the small text. Body charcoal ink, not an impersonal modern sans, not a digital interface font. One restrained hand-painted indigo initial letter at the start of the body gives the page life. Tiny antique ink stars and a slender orbital curve can accompany the heading; all decoration should come from the galaxy, not vines, castles or generic medieval scrollwork.
Exact visible Portuguese text on LEFT page, faithfully spelled, no additional copy:
Small rubric at top: "FASE I"
Main heading on two lines: "O primeiro" / "édito"
Short lead, slightly larger: "Uma carta. Uma ordem."
Body in short well-separated paragraphs:
"Vire a carta e guarde o número."
"Quando ela desaparecer, ande essa quantidade de casas."
Controls near the lower middle:
"W · A · S · D"
"Um passo por tecla."
Small discreet bottom note:
"Números romanos"
"Consulte a tabela no livro."
Do not invent extra paragraphs or numerical solutions. Keep the text readable and airy; retain generous blank paper between the title, body and controls.
RIGHT page: let the colored ink-and-watercolor plate occupy most of the page height with an irregular hand-painted edge and a slim clean paper margin. Preserve expressive contour lines, dry-brush and pigment granulation, matte printed colors, quiet indigo, amber and burgundy. No digital bloom, no glossy rendering, no photo of a screen. Small page numbers "1" and "2" centered at the bottom, no other text on the illustration. A refined tactile old illustrated fable book, coherent with the new cloth cover and cosmic game universe.
